newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Holomisa says S.Africa's ANC expels him.
newsitem.headline: Holomisa says S.Africa's ANC expels him.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress on Monday rejected an appeal by former deputy minister Bantu Holomisa against expulsion from the party, Holomisa said.

Holomisa, former deputy minister of tourism and environmental affairs, said in a telephone interview that participants in a meeting of the ANC's policy-making National Executive Committee (NEC) had told him of the decision.
"They have expelled me," he said. "My next step will be to challenge the whole process through the supreme court. Facts will be facts in a court of law."
An ANC disciplinary hearing in August kicked Holomisa out of the party for having brought it into disrepute by accusing it of accepting tainted money from a leading South African businessman.

Holomisa was military ruler of the nominally-independent black Transkei homeland before it was dismantled after all-race elections in April 1994 and is one of the most popular ANC leaders among grass-roots supporters.

Several thousand Holomisa supporters attended a rally he addressed in the former Transkei capital, Umtata, last week. About 200 people also marched on ANC headquarters in Johannesburg to demand that he remain in the party.
The ANC disciplinary committee said in its ruling last month that Holomisa had shown "no respect whatsoever" for the party.

"There is a tendency in this whole process... that he is above the organisation. He confuses his membership of the movement with his status as being a head of the bantustan of the Transkei," the committee said.
"He has turned the whole process into a public circus."

Holomisa's first corruption allegation was made during a hearing of the country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, when he said Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau had accepted a bribe of 50,000 rand ($11,000) from the businessman in the 1980s when she was part of the Transkei administration.
President Nelson Mandela later sacked Holomisa as deputy minister, giving no reasons.

In August Holomisa made further allegations, saying a businessman had given the ANC two million rand to fight the 1994 election and claimed at least two other ANC members had accepted favours from him.
Mandela confirmed the party had received the cash, but said there was nothing untoward about it. The party denied the other charges.
